Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0013", "row_sha256": "0ae1172059a155e50da205d5fbdfd88a733c079ece2996a280dc6fbe54b0ea7a", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, i'm putting together a handoff for our small lighting crew for saturday's matinee. could you write a short setup note, but only if the spare 19-degree Source Four is available and its lamp is working? the note should ask the crew to hang that fixture over the upstage doorway and aim it at the painted sign there, so the sign has a readable pool of light. the sign is used in the opening scene, and we want the note to be clear enough for the two-person crew to follow during setup. there's a blue tape mark on the floor for the temporary worklight, not for this fixture, so please don't mix those up. if the spare Source Four isn't available or its lamp doesn't work, don't write the setup note; instead, make a brief checklist for checking whether the existing side wash makes the sign readable from the back row. keep that fallback focused on checking the side wash, not on changing it. either way i need only the one item that applies, without a greeting or explanation. the person assigning this will confirm availability and lamp condition, so don't assume either one.", "output": "Prepare one item for the lighting crew for Saturday's matinee:

- If the spare 19-degree Source Four is available and its lamp is working, write a short setup note asking the crew to hang it over the upstage doorway and aim it at the painted sign for a readable pool of light. The sign appears in the opening scene. Do not confuse the blue floor tape mark for the temporary worklight with a mark for this fixture.
- If the fixture is unavailable or its lamp is not working, do not write the setup note. Instead, make a brief checklist for checking whether the existing side wash makes the sign readable from the back row. Keep the checklist focused on checking the side wash, not changing it.

Return only the applicable item, with no greeting or explanation. Availability and lamp condition will be confirmed by the person assigning this."}]
